# `silk/machine/paths`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Paths through a chart: how to reach each state, and which states cannot be reached.

## When to use
Use [`Paths.shortest`](#Paths.impl.shortest) to write one test per state without working out the events by hand,
and [`Paths.unreachable`](#Paths.impl.unreachable) in a test or a build step to catch a state that no transition
leads to.

## Details
A path is found in one chart of a `Definition`, from its initial state, with the fewest
steps. Every transition counts as possible, guarded or not, so a path says how a state can
be reached when the guards allow it. A step is the event's name, `always` for an eventless
transition, or `after <duration>` for a delayed one, such as `after 2s`. The transition
that any event takes is the step `*`.

## Gotchas
Regions are charts of their own. A path does not cross from a chart into the chart of a
region: ask for the region's chart by its name.

Import as `Paths` with `import silk.machine.paths { Paths }`.

<a id="Paths.impl.shortest"></a>

### Associated function `shortest`

```silk
pub effect fn shortest(definition: &Definition, chart: string) -> List<Path>
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns a shortest path to every state of the chart called `chart` that can be reached,
the initial state first. A chart the definition does not have gives no paths.

<a id="Paths.impl.unreachable"></a>

### Associated function `unreachable`

```silk
pub effect fn unreachable(definition: &Definition, chart: string) -> List<String>
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the names of the states of the chart called `chart` that no path reaches.
